hook: A city's bike-share system moves bikes between stations every day: most stay put, some are ridden across town. Knowing only the chances of each move, a matrix can predict how many bikes each station will have tomorrow, next week and in the long run, and even how many it had yesterday.

prereq.q: If $A\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{w}$ and $\det A \ne 0$, how do you find $\mathbf{v}$ from $\mathbf{w}$?
prereq.why: Multiply both sides on the left by $A^{-1}$: $A^{-1}A\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}$.

figure.caption: Each arrow is a daily chance. As a transition matrix with "from" columns and "to" rows: $\left[ \begin{matrix} 0.8 & 0.3 \\ 0.2 & 0.7 \end{matrix} \right]$.

chain.cause: List the chance of moving from each state (column) to each state (row)
chain.effect: the transition matrix $T$; each column adds up to $1$

chain.cause: Multiply the current state vector by $T$
chain.effect: the expected state one step later: $\mathbf{x}_{n+1} = T\mathbf{x}_n$
the state one step earlier, as long as $T$ has an inverse

ideas: A transition matrix $T$: the entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the chance of moving from state $j$ to state $i$ in one step. Each column adds up to $1$.
A state vector lists how many (or what share) are in each state. One step later: $\mathbf{x}_{n+1} = T\mathbf{x}_n$; after $n$ steps: $\mathbf{x}_n = T^n\mathbf{x}_0$.
A steady state satisfies $T\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{x}$. Over many steps the state vector usually settles toward it.

misconception.wrong: The first row of the bike matrix, $0.8$ and $0.3$, lists what happens to the bikes at station A.
misconception.right: With this setup the columns are "from" and the rows are "to". Column 1, $0.8$ and $0.2$, is what happens to bikes at A; row 1 collects every bike that ends at A. Always check which way your matrix is set up: each column adds up to 1 here.

summary: A transition matrix holds the chances of moving between states in one step, with "from" columns that add up to 1. Multiplying a state vector by $T$ moves it one step forward, $T^n$ moves it $n$ steps, $T^{-1}$ moves it one step back, and a steady state is a vector that $T$ leaves unchanged.
